p:cNvPr.descr: Structural representations of some protein kinase inhibitors. This diagram is shown in four phases: a) Imatinib (Gleevec) bound to Abl; b) Erlotinib (Tarceva) bound to EGF-R; c) ATP bound to CDK2; and d) Roscovatine bound to CDK2. This diagram is shown in four phases: (a) Imatinib (Gleevec) bound to Abl; (b) Erlotinib (Tarceva) bound to EGF-R; (c) ATP bound to CDK2; and (d) Roscovatine bound to CDK2. In diagram (a), there are several white and gray helices coiled with white and red loops indicated. At the center of the structure is an opaque structure that has blue, black, and red beads lined throughout. Below this image is a molecular structural representation of Imatinib (C29H31N7O). Diagram (b) shows a similar structure, but the red and white loops, as well as the opaque structure with the red, black, and blue beads, are much more pronounced. Below it, the structure of Tarceva (C22H23N3O4) is shown. Tarceva has a carbon ring bonded to a NH, which is bonded to another ring with nitrogens at the second and fourth positions. This ring is bound to another carbon ring, which is bound to an oxygen on each side of the bottom Carbons. Each Oxygen is bound to a Carbon, which is bound to another Carbon, which is bound to another oxygen. In diagram c, there are thick white and gray coils intertwined. Amongst the coils, there is are red and white loops, along with a gren mass in the center, and blue, black, and red beads held together by an opaque structure. Diagram d is similar to the others; however the opaque structure that holds the blue, black, and red beads is seen at the top of the image. Below it, there is a structural representation of Roscovatine (C19H26N6O). Roscovatine is comprised of a carbon ring conected to CHN, which is bound to a purine. The pentagon side of the purine is bound to C3H7. The hexagon side of the purine is bound to NH2, which is bound to CH, which is bound to CH2, which is bound to OH on the left. The same CH is bound to CH2, which is bound to CH3 on the right.
